questions.question: What happens to your original CSV file when you clean it in Power Query?

answerOptions.text: Power Query overwrites it with the cleaned data
answerOptions.rationale: The source is never changed.

answerOptions.text: It is moved into the workbook and deleted from the folder
answerOptions.rationale: The file stays where it is and is read again on refresh.

answerOptions.text: It is converted to .xlsx in the same folder
answerOptions.rationale: Power Query loads results into Excel; it does not convert the source.

answerOptions.text: It stays untouched; your cleaning is saved as steps that run again on Refresh
answerOptions.rationale: Power Query reads the source and records each fix as an applied step.

questions.question: After importing a CSV, product code 0733 shows as 733. What caused it, and what is the fix?

answerOptions.text: The CSV file is damaged; ask for a new export
answerOptions.rationale: The file is fine; the guessed data type dropped the zero.

answerOptions.text: The automatic Changed Type step made it a number; delete that step and keep the code as text
answerOptions.rationale: Never trust automatic types for codes, PIN codes or phone numbers.

answerOptions.text: Excel rounds codes; widen the column
answerOptions.rationale: Column width does not bring back a lost leading zero.

answerOptions.text: Use Remove Blank Rows
answerOptions.rationale: That removes empty lines; it does not change data types.

questions.question: Dates in the CSV are written day-month-year. How do you make sure Power Query reads them correctly on any Mac?

answerOptions.text: Set the Data Type to Text
answerOptions.rationale: Text keeps them as words, so they will not sort or group as dates.

answerOptions.text: Split the column by the dash delimiter
answerOptions.rationale: That breaks the date into pieces rather than converting it.

answerOptions.text: Control-click the column > Change Type > Using Locale, Date, English (India)
answerOptions.rationale: Using Locale reads the dates in the order you specify, whatever the Mac's region.

answerOptions.text: Leave the automatic Changed Type step as it is
answerOptions.rationale: The automatic guess can swap day and month.

questions.question: In a customer list, the Region is typed only once per group, with blanks (null) below it. Which command fills every row?

answerOptions.text: Transform > Fill > Down
answerOptions.rationale: Fill Down copies each value into the blank cells below it.

answerOptions.text: Home > Replace Values
answerOptions.rationale: Replace changes one value to another; it does not fill blanks from above.

answerOptions.text: Home > Remove Rows > Remove Blank Rows
answerOptions.rationale: That would drop rows instead of filling them.

answerOptions.text: Add Column > Conditional Column
answerOptions.rationale: A rule-based column does not copy the value from the row above.

questions.question: A budget has Region, Category and one column per month. What is the most reliable way to turn the months into rows?

answerOptions.text: Select the twelve month columns, then Unpivot Columns
answerOptions.rationale: It works today but leaves out any new column added later.

answerOptions.text: Select Region and Category, then Unpivot Other Columns
answerOptions.rationale: It keeps working when a new month column is added next year.

answerOptions.text: Use Pivot Column on Category
answerOptions.rationale: Pivot goes from tall to wide, the opposite direction.

answerOptions.text: Use Transpose on the whole table
answerOptions.rationale: Transpose swaps rows and columns, which does not give a tall Month and Sales layout.

questions.question: Your stacked sales list has only product codes. How do you bring in the product name and GST rate from the product master?

answerOptions.text: Append Queries with the product master
answerOptions.rationale: Append stacks rows; it does not add columns by key.

answerOptions.text: Use Fill Down on the Product Code column
answerOptions.rationale: Fill Down copies values downwards and adds no product details.

answerOptions.text: Merge Queries on Product Code with Left Outer, then Expand the new column
answerOptions.rationale: Merge joins on a key like XLOOKUP, and Expand pulls out the fields.

answerOptions.text: Load the product master as Only Create Connection and stop there
answerOptions.rationale: A connection alone does not join the two tables.

questions.question: After cleaning the Transform Sample File in a folder combine, the main query shows "The column Column1 was not found". What is the fix?

answerOptions.text: Delete the Changed Type step in the main query
answerOptions.rationale: That step still uses the old column names from before your cleaning.

answerOptions.text: Delete the Transform Sample File query
answerOptions.rationale: That query applies your cleaning to every file, so you need it.

answerOptions.text: Rename every CSV file in the folder
answerOptions.rationale: File names are not the cause of this error.

answerOptions.text: Remove the top four rows again in the main query
answerOptions.rationale: The rows are already removed in the sample; the old type step is the problem.

questions.question: A colleague asks you to build a Data Model with DAX measures in Excel for Mac. What should you tell them?

answerOptions.text: Turn on Power Pivot from Tools > Excel Add-ins
answerOptions.rationale: There is no Power Pivot add-in for Excel for Mac.

answerOptions.text: Choose Load to Data Model in Close & Load To
answerOptions.rationale: Load to Data Model is not available in Power Query on Mac.

answerOptions.text: Show it from Excel > Preferences > Ribbon & Toolbar
answerOptions.rationale: No ribbon setting adds Power Pivot to the Mac.

answerOptions.text: Mac Excel cannot create or edit a Data Model, so use Power BI Desktop or Excel for Windows
answerOptions.rationale: Power Pivot, the Data Model and DAX are not available on Mac.
